files.content:
# Pixel Memory Match

A simple offline memory game built with HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.

## How to run
Open `index.html` in any modern browser. No server, install, or network connection required.

## How to play
- Click or tap a card to flip it.
- Flip two cards at a time.
- If the colors match, the pair stays open.
- If they do not match, they flip back after a short delay.
- The move counter goes up after each pair of flips.
- Match all 8 pairs to see the win message.
- Use the **New Game** button to shuffle and restart.

## Keyboard access
- Press `Tab` to move between the New Game button and cards.
- Press `Enter` or `Space` to activate buttons.
- Each card has an accessible label announcing its position and color.

output.goal: Build an offline browser memory-match game with 8 pairs of colored cards, flip-two-at-a-time matching, move counting, win message, and a New game button using only HTML, CSS, and plain JavaScript.

phases.name: Foundation & structure
tasks: Create root index.html with centered game board container and accessible control regions
Create styles.css with a cohesive 3-5 color palette and base layout
Write README.md with project overview, run instructions, and keyboard usage

phases.name: Core game logic
tasks: Implement 8 pairs of colored cards and shuffle them on load
Handle flipping two cards at a time and comparing matches
Keep matched pairs open and reset non-matches after a short delay
Track move count and detect win condition after all pairs are matched
Show win message and implement New game button reset behavior

phases.name: UI styling & responsive layout
tasks: Style centered card/game board on a themed background
Draw card graphics with CSS or canvas, including color pairs
Add visible hover, focus, and pressed states for controls
Ensure layout works from 360px wide using system fonts at 16px or larger
Polish visual hierarchy, spacing, and finished appearance

phases.name: Accessibility, acceptance & final checks
tasks: Add keyboard-accessible labeled controls and manage focus order
Verify addEventListener is used instead of inline HTML event handlers
Test offline browser behavior at desktop and mobile widths
Confirm all file paths are relative and use .html, .css, .js, .md extensions
Validate win message, move count, and New game button against acceptance criteria

risks: Rapid card clicks may cause state desynchronization or allow more than two flipped cards
Styling could accidentally hide required card text, IDs, or keyboard focus indicators
Responsive card sizing may fail at exactly 360px if dimensions are too rigid
Keyboard accessibility may be missed without manual testing
Keeping all graphics internal with CSS/canvas may increase implementation time
